stdout: usage: bale open [-h] [--verbose] [--no-sandbox] [--check | --dry-run] bundle
Consume a planner bundle (.bale-bundle; BALE.md §6.7) and pack its session,
cheapest gate first, every refusal landing before any session state exists.
(1) Gate bundle.json through validate_bundle_manifest before trusting anything
else, and verify each member's published sha256 against its LF-normalized
bytes. (2) Parse the stored pack argv with the real CLI parser and run every
argv-only pack gate — flag pairs, the brief and checkpoint reads, the include-
naming checkpoint gate, the supersession guards, forecast existence and
disjointness; the same implementations `bale pack` runs (boards 68, 122) — so
a bundle the replay would refuse on its argv alone refuses here, in that
gate's own words, with no dry-run spent; refusals name the resolved project
root and the config files judged. (3) When the bundle ships a checkpoint,
refuse up front if the project pins no [validation] base, then dry-run the
checkpoint read-only against a scratch copy of the live base and echo the
expected-HOLD proof (exit 1 expected; exit 2 refuses the whole open as a
defective oracle; exit 0 proceeds with a vacuous-oracle warning). (4) Replay
the stored pack argv with --readme-file/--no-readme and --checkpoint-file
supplied from member presence and the bundle's pre_answered intents riding the
in-process channel — routed through every decline-default exchange, never
around it. The replayed pack re-runs every gate at its own site; the early
gates are a cost ordering, not a substitute. --check and --dry-run rehearse a
prefix of this pipeline and write nothing (v0.4.45).
positional arguments:
bundle        Path to the planner bundle (.bale-bundle). A relative path
resolves like apply's tarball argument: cwd first, then each
configured apply.search_paths directory in order; an absolute
path bypasses the search.
options:
-h, --help    show this help message and exit
--verbose     Stream the checkpoint dry-run's output live instead of
capturing it and echoing the probe-verdict lines.
--no-sandbox  Run the checkpoint dry-run UNCONFINED for this invocation
(ADR-0016 escape; same semantics as `bale apply --no-sandbox`,
scoped here to the dry-run — the replayed pack executes no
scripts). Per-invocation only, and every use is FORCE-logged;
bale.toml's project-layer [sandbox] enabled = false (v0.4.26)
unconfines the dry-run durably, FORCE-logged naming the key,
and this flag is redundant beside it.
--check       Rehearse steps (1)-(2) and stop (v0.4.45): verify the bundle
and run every argv-only pack gate against the live tree — the
include-naming checkpoint gate among them. Exit 0 when every
gate passes. Spends no oracle and writes nothing.
--dry-run     Rehearse steps (1)-(3) and stop (v0.4.45): --check, then the
checkpoint dry-run against the live base exactly as an open
runs it, verdict lines echoed and its log kept in a temp
directory outside the repo. Exit 0 when the gates pass and the
oracle exits 0 or 1 (an expected HOLD); nonzero when a gate
refuses or the oracle exits 2. Writes nothing.
